listing.name: Atomic Bomberman (Atomic Bomberman — Modern)
listing.summary: A native Atomic Bomberman recreation with its own generated graphics and sound.

steps.title: Start the Atomic Bomberman player
steps.instruction: Use atomic.exe from the v1.0 modern Windows x64 ZIP or atomic from the modern Linux x86-64 tar.gz. Choose the player package. The dedicated server is a separate program. The player can generate free assets without original files.

steps.title: Check Linux graphics and libraries
steps.instruction: Use an OpenGL 3.3 driver, glibc 2.38 or later, and libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.31. SDL3 is built into this Linux package.

warnings: Keep the whole effective SDL profile, imported assets and custom files before updating. A second copy normally shares the same user profile.

references.title: Use original assets if desired
references.instruction: Follow upstream to import from your own copy of Atomic Bomberman. Preserve the original files and the SDL profile, normally ~/.local/share/atomic-bomberman-modern/atomic on Linux or %APPDATA%/atomic-bomberman-modern/atomic on Windows. Free assets can fall back to the player working directory when the profile is unavailable.

presentation.manual_preparation: Start atomic.exe on Windows or atomic on Linux. The dedicated server is a separate program. No original game files are required for the code-generated free asset set. An OpenGL 3.3 graphics driver is required. The Linux x86-64 package needs glibc 2.38 or later and libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.31. Optional original Atomic Bomberman (1997) data and --import-assets preparation remain upstream/player-owned; do not treat an engine install as permission to acquire that content. The normal writable SDL profile for atomic-bomberman-modern/atomic holds options.ini, schemes, anims.lst and imported/generated assets under the current account’s AppData on Windows or data home on Linux; copies share it and Core does not back it up, migrate or delete it. If preference lookup fails, free assets fall back to free-assets beside the creating player; Core retains this declared local directory, including unknown/custom files during its maintenance. Upstream rewrites its known generated files when the free-assets version changes; its free-assets.txt marker is internal, not a Core completion or save-compatibility certificate. Failed profile lookup disables normal settings persistence and can send editor scheme saves to a root-relative /name.sch path outside the engine. Stop editor saving and repair the profile upstream if that occurs; preserve any actual external outputs. This managed offer requires the normal writable profile, does not sandbox the player and does not claim free-assets captures every fault output. Preserve the whole creating runtime, all effective profiles, custom files and originals before changes. No actual game, editor, import or network behavior is qualified.
